claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 873 m (F1), he never came within 200 m (F1), and the platform never recorded him at the pickup (driver_arrived_at is null, F4).

The rider's own messages show she was at the pickup point and could see no car (F9 at 22:38), and the driver's later "I waited at the pickup" statement (F12) is contradicted by the GPS record, so the system records win and no no-show by the rider is established.

The rider has 1 dispute in 90 days (F16), which the driver may use to portray her as a disputatious complainant, though 0 were upheld (F16).

Chat message F8 (22:37, driver: "Reached already") is a driver claim of arrival; it conflicts with GPS (F1, F5) and the platform record (F4), so it loses, but the judge may still note there was some contact at the stated time.

No traffic or route facts explain the driver's position (F13, F14) — this is neutral for the rider but leaves no alternative explanation for why he was 1000 m away; light rain (F15) is the only outside factor and does not excuse a 1000 m mis-tap under NS-1.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 22:37:20, which is the arrival confirmation the policy requires as element (i) of a valid no-show cancellation. (See weakness W1: the tap does not satisfy element (ii).)

GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point in the whole trip was 873 m at 22:36:00 and he never came within 200 m, and the platform's own record confirms driver_arrived_at is null, so NS-1 (ii) is not met.

At the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was 1000 m from the pickup point and he spent 0 s within 200 m afterwards; his stationary period of 5 min 0 s from 22:37:00 to 22:42:00 was at a point 1000 m from the pickup, so the waiting in NS-1 (iii) did not occur at the pickup point and cannot satisfy that element.

The driver's post-hoc statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system GPS and timeline records, which the policy ranks above a statement alone, so the statement cannot establish the location element of the no-show.

The driver's own chat message at 22:37 says "Reached already" while the GPS put him 1000 m away at that moment, and the rider replied at 22:38 that she was at the pickup point with no car there; the record therefore shows the driver was not at the pickup and the no-show is not made out on the system records.

The rider's location claim is corroborated by the fact that the platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point at any time before the cancellation, which is consistent with her account that she waited there.

The driver cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance, at 22:42:00, and the $6.61 cancellation fee is on record; because the no-show conditions are not satisfied the fee does not stand and must be fully refunded to the rider (refund_full).

There is no traffic or incident record near the optimal route during the trip window; the only environmental factor is light rain (1.8 mm), which does not excuse the driver's position at the time of the "I'm Here" tap.

The chat record is complete (3 messages, all timestamped), so the case does not fall into the incomplete-record escalation in the missing-evidence rule; the facts are sufficient to decide the no-show question on the records.

We do not request a flag_account against the rider: her account is 1298 days old with one dispute and none upheld, so there is no profile basis for an account action against her; the profile facts are used only for this request, not to decide the case.

weaknesses: W1 — The driver did press "I'm Here" (F5) and did wait five minutes (F2), and he stated he waited at the pickup (F12); the other side will point to these as evidence of good faith, but the same records (F1, F4, F5) put him 1000 m from the pickup, so the location element fails regardless.

W2 — The driver's 22:37 message "Reached already" (F8) is contradicted by GPS (F1, F2); this is an unhelpful record for our client and the judge may read it unfavourably, but it does not create an NS-1 (ii) compliance.

W3 — Our client's driver profile shows 2 disputes upheld in 90 days, both no-show type (F17); this is a genuine risk that the judge adds a flag_account or escalates for the driver's account, even though profile facts cannot decide the case alone.
